claims.text: The initial alloy contains Al, Co, Cr, Fe, and Ni.
The initial alloy has a continuous dual-phase lamellar microstructure.
The initial alloy exhibits catastrophic interfacial cracking and low ductility under room-temperature uniaxial tension.
Hydrostatic pressure above 5 GPa combined with shear deformation at 0.4–0.6 Tm will fragment the continuous lamellar structure.
The treatment will produce a patterned, equiaxed, or wavy interface topology with increased interface curvature and reduced lamellar aspect ratio.
Fragmenting the continuous interfaces will eliminate long-range stress concentrators.
The patterned interface topology will promote uniform plasticity.
Extreme hydrostatic pressure suppresses void nucleation at phase interfaces.
Extreme hydrostatic pressure suppresses crack propagation at phase interfaces.
Shear deformation induces lamellar fragmentation.
Shear deformation induces dynamic recrystallization.
Breaking the continuity of phase interfaces enables dislocation cross-slip across phase boundaries.
The proposed treatment will significantly increase uniform elongation.
The proposed treatment will significantly increase total ductility.
The proposed treatment will maintain or enhance yield strength.
The treated alloy will not exhibit catastrophic interfacial cracking under room-temperature uniaxial tension.
Conventional HIP below 2 GPa without applied shear typically preserves or slightly coarsens the lamellar structure.
A pressure above 5 GPa is the critical threshold needed to suppress brittle fracture mechanisms.
Keeping the treatment temperature below the eutectic melting point avoids gross phase dissolution.
Excessive treatment temperature can produce grain growth that causes the treatment to fail.

contradictions.description: The intervention and boundary require pressure above 5 GPa, but the proposed Group A treatment uses exactly 5 GPa, which does not satisfy a strict >5 GPa threshold.
